open_points.subject: create replay after an ordinary change to the created record
open_points.text: This holds while the record the first create made keeps its values
open_points.question: Which changes make a created record stop "keeping its values": only erasure or anonymisation that removes its create request id, or also ordinary corrections and lifecycle changes such as archiving, restriction, or ending a relationship; and after such an ordinary change does a retry return the existing record, create another record, or get refused?
options: Replay protection lasts while the create request id remains, including after ordinary corrections and lifecycle changes.
Any change to a create-time value ends replay protection, so the repeated request is a new create.
A changed record is still recognised, but the repeated create is refused because its original content no longer equals the current record.
open_points.default_guess: Replay protection lasts until erasure or anonymisation removes the stored create request id; ordinary changes do not turn the retry into a new create.

witness.initial: Customer C was recorded with request id Q and revision 1.
events: The owner corrects C's phone number, moving it to revision 2.
The owner interface later repeats the original record-customer request with Q.
outcomes: Registry recognises Q and returns C as the result of the original create, making no second Customer.
Because C no longer keeps its original values, Registry treats Q as a new create and mints Customer C2; alternatively it refuses the request as unequal to C.
witness.observer: The owner sees either one Customer, two Customers, or a refusal.

open_points.subject: project-create replay after whole project deletion
open_points.text: Erasing a customer or anonymising a project removes everything that would tell a repeat; a create repeated after that is a new create
open_points.question: Does deleting an archived project whole, rather than anonymising it, also end recognition of its original project-create request and make a later repeat a new create?
options: Whole deletion behaves like anonymisation: the repeated project create is new and Registry mints a new project.
Only anonymisation has the stated exception; whole deletion must retain or otherwise honour the original no-duplicate replay guarantee.
A retry after whole deletion is recognised but refused instead of creating or returning a project.
open_points.default_guess: Whole deletion also removes replay recognition, so the repeated request creates a new project.

witness.initial: Active project P was created with request id Q.
events: The owner confirms deletion of P whole.
The owner interface repeats the original create-project request with Q.
outcomes: Registry treats Q as new and creates active project P2 with a newly minted identity.
Registry continues treating Q as the original create and therefore makes no second project, returning a refusal or another non-creating result.
witness.observer: The owner and project-list consumers see whether a new project exists.

open_points.subject: room-create replay after its project is anonymised
open_points.text: Erasing a customer or anonymising a project removes everything that would tell a repeat; a create repeated after that is a new create, and its answer shows the new record it made.
open_points.question: Does this rule cover a repeated room create whose Room and request id disappeared when its project was anonymised, or only the create of the Customer or Project that was itself erased or anonymised?
options: It applies only to the erased Customer's record-customer request and the anonymised Project's create-project request; a room retry is refused because its project is erased and archived.
It applies to every create record removed by anonymisation, including a Room, so the retry must create a new Room despite the project's normal erased-project refusal.
The room request is treated as fresh because replay evidence is gone, but normal project preconditions are then applied and it is refused.
open_points.default_guess: The exception applies only to creation of the Customer or Project itself; a repeated add-room request is refused for the anonymised project.

witness.initial: Active project P contains room R, created with request id Q.
events: The owner anonymises P, which removes its rooms and their request ids.
Cabinet Kernel repeats the add-room request Q for P on behalf of the formerly granted session.
outcomes: The request is refused because P is anonymised, archived, and no longer granted; no Room is made.
The new replay sentence is applied to the removed Room record, so Registry treats Q as a new create and answers with a newly minted Room.
witness.observer: The owner and Kernel see whether the request is refused or a Room is created on an anonymised project.
